title: The Parrot Manifesto
summary: The longest study of human happiness says a good life is other people. Parrot exists to be beautifully human.
body_markdown:
What makes a good life?


Money? A big career? Fame? Good genes?


In 1938, Harvard started[the longest study of human happiness](https://www.adultdevelopmentstudy.org/) . It has run from 1938 to 2026, and it is still going. Three generations. The directors told the story in *The Good Life* , in 2023.


The study began with 724 young men, from two different worlds. 268 were Harvard sophomores. 456 were boys from inner-city Boston. The study followed them for their whole lives. Today it includes about 2,500 people: their wives, their children, and their grandchildren.


One of those Harvard students became President of the United States. John F. Kennedy was in the study. So was Ben Bradlee, the editor who ran The Washington Post.


The study had money, fame, and power in it. Did they make people happy?


The happiest people did not have the most money, career success, fame, IQ, or good genes. They had the best relationships.


Robert Waldinger, the director, said it in one line. "Good relationships keep us happier and healthier. Period."


The people most satisfied with their relationships at 50 were the healthiest at 80. That beat cholesterol as a predictor. Loneliness is as bad for your health as smoking half a pack of cigarettes a day.


How do people connect? We listen. We speak.


Every relationship starts with a conversation. The study says even a short chat with the barista makes us a little happier.


You can't connect with someone you can't understand.


That is the gap. A 400-day streak on a language app. Then the barista, at normal speed. Most apps teach words. Real life is listening.


Parrot closes that gap. Real people. Real voices. Real speed.


Our purpose is connecting people. Language is how we start.


How do we help people connect in real life? On a flight. At an Airbnb. At a hotel. In a coffee shop. At a concert.


Every one of those moments starts with listening and speaking. That is where Parrot begins.


The companies people love can say who they are in a few words.


Apple: Think different.


Nike: Just do it.


Starbucks: Inspire and nurture the human spirit.


Spotify: Music for everyone.


Pinterest: Inspiration to create a life you love.


Airbnb: Belong anywhere.


Mastercard: Priceless.


McDonald's: I'm lovin' it.


Coca-Cola: Real magic.


L'Oréal: Because you're worth it.


Red Bull: Red Bull gives you wings.


BMW: The ultimate driving machine.


Google: Organize the world's information.


Disneyland: The happiest place on Earth.


Instagram: Bring you closer to the people and things you love.


TED: Ideas worth spreading.


Patagonia: We're in business to save our home planet.


Microsoft: Empower every person to achieve more.


And Parrot?


**Beautifully human.**
